meta.description: Detect and remove doublets (two or more cells in one droplet) from single-cell RNA-seq using scDblFinder (R), Scrublet (Python), and DoubletFinder (R). Use when flagging artificial intermediate populations before clustering, setting the expected doublet rate from recovered-cell counts, running detection per sample before integration, choosing between simulate-and-score methods, or interpreting a non-bimodal score histogram.

scientific_integrity.detail: Every number reported back came from a logged run (run/*.log). The eight cited references are real and correctly attributed; the Skill's claim that the Xi and Li 2021 ranking is superseded was tested rather than repeated and held (scDblFinder AUC 0.977 vs DoubletFinder 0.685 on the same lane).

practice_boundaries.detail: No output diagnoses, prescribes or triages an individual. The Skill works on count matrices only.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled fallacy. The stress input invited the classic error - calling a CD3D+LYZ+ cluster a novel transitional cell type - and the response tested it for doublet enrichment against a dataset-wide baseline before refusing the claim.

code_usability.detail: All 5 inputs executed. The SKILL.md scDblFinder and Scrublet blocks run; DoubletFinder runs when called as SKILL.md:123 prints it. Two defects found - the Scrublet per-sample loop at SKILL.md:105 writes to a view and silently loses its results, and examples/doubletfinder.R:36 aborts with 'cannot xtfrm data frames' - but each has a one-token fix and the primary path runs, so these are P1 items, not an M4 failure.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 4: all three named methods have code, plus the rate rule, the multiplexed-lane rule, and the heterotypic/homotypic/neotypic table; solo and scds are explicitly secondary. Correctness 3: nearly every factual claim was verified true in execution (per-sample beats merged, precision 0.693 vs 0.534; scDblFinder beats DoubletFinder, AUC 0.977 vs 0.685; *_v3 names really are gone; homotypic doublets really are invisible, 0/25 recovered on a sorted population), but the Python per-sample loop at SKILL.md:105 operates on a view and its results never reach the parent object. Appropriateness 4.

reliability.note: Fault tolerance 3: Category 3 Override 1 says to score on whether failures are caught and reported clearly - and the two failures this audit hit were both SILENT or misdiagnosed. The view loop raises only an ImplicitModificationWarning and produces an object with no doublet columns at all. Error reporting 3: the 9-row Common Errors table is good, but its DoubletFinder row prescribes 'use current function names', which does not fix the error the shipped example actually raises. Recoverability 3: flag-and-inspect rather than delete is the right recoverable design and is stated twice.

performance_context.note: Token cost 3: 164 lines, the tightest of the single-cell Skills audited here, no duplicated code paths, but no references/ layer. Execution efficiency 4: one decision table, one method per section, no redundant steps.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 4, consistency 4 and error prevention 4 are all strong - the Governing Principle is three numbered facts, each of which this audit confirmed empirically. Feedback design 3: no output format or checkpoint is specified; the agent has to decide what to report.

human_usability.note: Discoverability 4: 'Remove doublets from my data' is exactly how the request arrives, and the usage guide covers the multiplexed-pool phrasing. Forgiveness 3: strict input handling is not penalised under Category 3 Override 2, but nothing tells the agent what to do when the sample key is missing from the object.

security.note: Credential safety 4: no credentials, no eval/exec, no network calls. Input validation 3: the Skill insists on raw counts and per-sample keys but gives no check that the object actually holds counts. Data safety 3: no note on donor-level data, though hashing/demultiplexing is discussed as a cross-sample doublet source.

maintainability.note: Modularity 4: one section per method, each Goal/Approach/code, plus six explicit Related Skills hand-offs. Modifiability 3. Testability 2: of the two shipped example scripts, examples/doubletfinder.R aborts on its own prescribed call (reuse.pANN = FALSE), so half the shipped verification surface does not execute, and there are no expected outputs to check a run against.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision 4, composability 4, escape hatches 4 (flag-and-inspect, 'do not claim doublet-free', hashing as complementary truth). Progressive disclosure 3. Idempotency 1: the Skill's headline call scDblFinder(sce, samples=...) is NOT reproducible under set.seed - two identically seeded runs disagreed on 54 cells, 22.7% of the union of their doublet calls - and the Skill gives no seed guidance anywhere. BPPARAM = SerialParam(RNGseed=) fixed it completely (0 disagreements) and is never mentioned.

inputs.label: scDblFinder per sample on 8 PBMC lanes, ground-truth scored
inputs.note: The Skill's headline claim is confirmed with numbers: samples= gives precision 0.693 vs 0.534 for the merged call, at AUC 0.977. The discovery is that the prescribed call is not reproducible under set.seed.
inputs.execution_note: run/input1.R, run/input1b_determinism.R, logs alongside. scDblFinder 1.20.2, Seurat 5.5.0, SYNTHETIC 8-sample PBMC set (6,524 cells, 195 injected doublets).

assertions.text: Running scDblFinder with samples= outperforms the merged call the Skill warns against
assertions.note: 215 calls at precision 0.693 / recall 0.764, vs 298 calls at precision 0.534 / recall 0.815 merged. The Skill's Common Errors row 1 is quantitatively correct.

assertions.text: The expected rate comes from each lane's recovered-cell count, not a package default
assertions.note: Printed per lane (0.57%-0.72% for 707-902 cells) alongside the injected 2.95%-3.06%, and the discrepancy is attributed to the dataset's deliberate over-loading rather than hidden.

assertions.text: Re-running the prescribed call with the same seed reproduces the same doublet calls
assertions.note: set.seed(20260916) twice gave 215 and 207 calls disagreeing on 54 cells - 22.7% of the union. BiocParallel::SerialParam(RNGseed=) gave 0 disagreements; the Skill never mentions either.

assertions.text: No claim is made that the dataset is doublet-free after removal
assertions.note: 46 of 195 injected doublets were missed and the response says so, following the Skill's 'report only the detectable fraction'.

inputs.label: Scrublet in scanpy, per sample, rate from recovered cells
inputs.note: The rate rule and the batch_key alternative both work and the batch_key route matched an explicit loop on 6524/6524 cells. The per-sample loop the Skill actually prints does not: it writes to a view and the parent object ends with no doublet columns.
inputs.execution_note: run/input2.py, run/input2b_view.py, logs alongside. scanpy 1.12.4. Scrublet AUC 0.869 against the injected truth, below scDblFinder's 0.977, consistent with the Skill's method ranking.

assertions.text: The per-sample loop the Skill prints writes its results back to the object being analysed
assertions.note: sc.pp.scrublet(adata[adata.obs.sample == s], ...) raises only ImplicitModificationWarning; 'doublet_score' and 'predicted_doublet' are both absent from the parent .obs afterwards. An agent following SKILL.md:105 literally ends with an unscored dataset it believes is scored.

assertions.text: expected_doublet_rate is set from recovered cells rather than Scrublet's 0.05 placeholder
assertions.note: Per-lane rates 0.0057-0.0072 used; the 0.05 placeholder was run as a comparison and gave 59 calls vs 47, confirming the Skill's point that it is a placeholder, not a recommendation.

assertions.text: The batch_key alternative the Skill offers in the same sentence gives the same answer as an explicit loop
assertions.note: Identical on all 6,524 cells; the alternative is sound even though the loop as printed is not.

assertions.text: Recall is reported against the actually injected rate rather than the rule's prediction
assertions.note: Recall 0.236 reported plainly, with the reason (the dataset injects ~3% per 800-cell lane, four times what the 0.8%/1000 rule predicts) stated as dataset context, not as a Skill defect.

inputs.label: FACS-sorted CD4 T cells - one population, is the doublet call meaningful?
inputs.note: The Skill's hardest claim tested in its worst case and validated: on 900 sorted CD4 T cells containing 25 real doublets, both the auto threshold and a rate-anchored manual threshold recovered ZERO of them.
inputs.execution_note: run/input3.py, run/input3.log; derived data at data/sorted_cd4.h5ad (SYNTHETIC, derivation in data/README.md). Auto threshold 0.0447 called 5 cells, all false positives; manual threshold from the rate rule called 20, all false positives.

assertions.text: The score distribution is inspected rather than the auto threshold being trusted
assertions.note: Simulated and observed score ranges printed and compared; the threshold sits above the observed maximum of most true doublets.

assertions.text: The homotypic-invisibility caveat is stated instead of reporting a doublet-free population
assertions.note: 18 of the 25 true CD4-CD4 doublets score above the median observed score but none cross any defensible threshold; the response reports the detectable fraction as zero rather than the doublet count as zero.

assertions.text: The manual-threshold fix the Skill prescribes is actually applied and its result reported
assertions.note: Applied with the only anchor the Skill offers (the expected rate); result recall 0.000, precision 0.000, reported rather than suppressed.

assertions.text: No conclusion is drawn that this sorted population is clean
assertions.note: The response recommends hashing/MULTI-seq as the complementary filter, which is the Skill's own escape hatch.

inputs.label: Legacy DoubletFinder route on an existing Seurat pipeline
inputs.note: The shipped example script aborts on its own call. The SKILL.md snippet (which omits reuse.pANN) works. The Skill's characterisation of DoubletFinder as brittle and second-best is confirmed: pANN AUC 0.685 vs scDblFinder 0.977 on the same lane.
inputs.execution_note: run/input4.R, run/input4.log. DoubletFinder 2.0.6 + Seurat 5.5.0. examples/doubletfinder.R:36 passes reuse.pANN = FALSE; because FALSE is not NULL, doubletFinder takes its reuse branch, does pANN.old <- seu@meta.data[, FALSE] (a zero-column data.frame) and dies in order() with 'Error in xtfrm.data.frame(x): cannot xtfrm data frames'.

assertions.text: The shipped example script runs as written on a standard 10x lane
assertions.note: examples/doubletfinder.R aborts at line 36 with 'cannot xtfrm data frames'. The Skill's Common Errors fix for DoubletFinder errors ('use current function names') does not address it - the names were already current.

assertions.text: The Skill's API-drift claim is verified against the installed package rather than assumed
assertions.note: ls('package:DoubletFinder') shows doubletFinder, paramSweep, find.pK, modelHomotypic, summarizeSweep and no *_v3 names, exactly as SKILL.md:114 and the method table state.

assertions.text: pK is swept per dataset instead of a default being reused
assertions.note: paramSweep + find.pK ran in 13.6 s and selected pK = 0.18 from the BCmvn maximum, as SKILL.md:116-118 prescribes.

assertions.text: The method's accuracy is compared with the recommended default rather than asserted
assertions.note: pANN AUC 0.685 on the same lane where scDblFinder scored 0.977; the Skill's 'do not cite Xi and Li 2021 against current scDblFinder' instruction is supported by the measurement.

inputs.label: 8 HTO-hashed donors in one lane, and a CD3D+LYZ+ cluster the PI wants to publish
inputs.note: The multiplexed-lane rule is validated (total-lane 5.22% vs per-sample 0.65% against a true 2.99%). The refusal of the 'novel transitional state' claim is correct, but the Skill's prescribed marker heuristic on its own would have pointed the wrong way.
inputs.execution_note: run/input5.py, run/input5.log. 20 Leiden clusters on the pooled SYNTHETIC set. Cluster 6 carries 13.0% true doublets against a 3.0% baseline (4.3x enriched), but is only 26.3% CD3D+LYZ+ against a 36.0% dataset-wide baseline - ambient RNA makes bare lineage co-expression useless here, which the Skill flags only in its Deeper Cautions paragraph, not next to the heuristic.

assertions.text: The expected rate is set from total lane loading, not from the demultiplexed subset
assertions.note: Both computed and contrasted: 0.65% per demultiplexed sample vs 5.22% from the 6,524-cell lane, against a true 2.99%. The Skill's direction is right and its magnitude is the closer of the two.

assertions.text: The candidate 'novel transitional' cluster is tested for doublet enrichment before any claim is made
assertions.note: Per-cluster true-doublet percentage computed for all 20 clusters; cluster 6 at 13.0% vs the 3.0% baseline identified as the doublet-suspect population.

assertions.text: No novel cell type is claimed from a doublet-enriched cluster
assertions.note: The claim is refused; hashing-based cross-sample doublet calling is recommended as confirmation, per the Skill's own Related Skills hand-off.

assertions.text: The lineage co-expression heuristic is checked against a dataset-wide baseline instead of used bare
assertions.note: Checked and found misleading here (26.3% in the suspect cluster vs 36.0% overall), and reported as a limitation of the heuristic under ambient contamination.

key_strengths: Every substantive factual claim in this Skill was tested in execution and held: per-sample beats merged (precision 0.693 vs 0.534), scDblFinder beats DoubletFinder (AUC 0.977 vs 0.685), homotypic doublets are invisible (0 of 25 recovered on a sorted population), the *_v3 names really are gone, and doublet score really does track total counts (r = 0.634).
The Governing Principle is three concrete, falsifiable statements rather than advice, and each one is the reason for a specific instruction later in the Skill.
The multiplexed-pool rule (set the rate from total lane loading, not the demultiplexed subset) is a mistake researchers make constantly, and the Skill states it with a worked number.

The escape hatches are unusually good for this domain: flag-and-inspect over deletion, never claim doublet-free, cross-check removed cells against cell-cycle signatures, and use hashing as complementary experimental truth.

recommendations.title: The Python per-sample loop silently discards its own results
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md:105 tells the agent to loop sc.pp.scrublet(adata[adata.obs.sample == s], ...). That indexes a view; scanpy raises only an ImplicitModificationWarning and the parent object ends with neither doublet_score nor predicted_doublet. The pipeline then continues as though doublets had been scored.
recommendations.root_cause: The loop was written as prose shorthand and never run; scanpy's view semantics make it a no-op rather than an error.
recommendations.fix: Replace the loop with one that collects results explicitly (sub = adata[mask].copy(); sc.pp.scrublet(sub, ...); adata.obs.loc[mask, 'doublet_score'] = sub.obs['doublet_score']) or lead with the batch_key form, which this audit verified agrees with an explicit loop on every cell. Add a Common Errors row: 'doublet columns missing after the per-sample loop -> scored a view'.

recommendations.title: The prescribed scDblFinder call is not reproducible and the Skill says nothing about seeds
recommendations.problem: scDblFinder(sce, samples = 'sample_id') under set.seed(20260916) gave 215 calls on one run and 207 on the next, disagreeing on 54 cells - 22.7% of the union of the two call sets. Which cells get deleted therefore changes between runs of the same script.
recommendations.root_cause: samples= dispatches through BiocParallel, which does not inherit the base R seed; the Skill has no seed guidance anywhere in SKILL.md, the usage guide or either example.
recommendations.fix: Add BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam(RNGseed = <seed>) to the prescribed call - it gave 0 disagreements across repeat runs here - and add one line to the Skill saying that set.seed() alone does not control it.

recommendations.title: Shipped DoubletFinder example aborts on its own call
recommendations.problem: examples/doubletfinder.R:36 calls doubletFinder(..., reuse.pANN = FALSE). Because FALSE is not NULL, DoubletFinder 2.0.6 takes its reuse branch, builds pANN.old from a zero-column data.frame and dies with 'Error in xtfrm.data.frame(x): cannot xtfrm data frames'.
recommendations.root_cause: reuse.pANN is a character column name or NULL, never a logical; the example was written as though FALSE meant 'do not reuse'.
recommendations.fix: Delete reuse.pANN = FALSE from examples/doubletfinder.R (the SKILL.md:123 snippet already omits it and runs), and add the error string to the Common Errors DoubletFinder row, whose current fix - 'use current function names' - does not address it.

recommendations.title: The lineage co-expression heuristic needs an ambient caveat where it is stated
recommendations.problem: The Governing Principle says to treat any small cluster co-expressing two lineage programs (CD3+LYZ) as doublet-suspect. On an ambient-contaminated dataset the genuinely doublet-enriched cluster was BELOW the dataset-wide CD3D+LYZ+ rate (26.3% vs 36.0%), so the heuristic points away from the right cluster.
recommendations.root_cause: The ambient caveat exists but is 100 lines away in Deeper Cautions, not attached to the heuristic it invalidates.
recommendations.fix: Add one clause where the heuristic is stated: compare co-expression against the dataset-wide rate, and run ambient removal first, or use the doublet score rather than raw co-expression.

recommendations.title: No guidance on what to report
recommendations.problem: The Skill specifies no output format. Each input required the agent to invent what to print, and the numbers that matter (per-sample call counts, threshold, detectable fraction) are exactly the ones a reviewer will ask for.
recommendations.root_cause: Feedback design is not covered anywhere in SKILL.md or the usage guide.
recommendations.fix: Add a four-line 'what to report' block: per-sample cell count, expected rate and where it came from, threshold used and whether it was automatic, and calls as a count and a percentage, with the homotypic caveat attached.
